title: The finite-stage colimit of bounded finite-dimensional derived categories
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and fix a prime $\ell\neq p$. Write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$ the field of $\ell$-adic numbers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $\Qlb$ a fixed algebraic closure of $\Ql$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and $\mathcal E_\ell$ the directed set of finite intermediate extensions $\Ql\subseteq E\subseteq\Qlb$, ordered by inclusion [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Work in a universe containing the derived categories $D(E)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and their morphism groups. For $E\in\mathcal E_\ell$, let $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)\subset D(E)$ be the full subcategory of objects with bounded finite-dimensional cohomology [def-weil-point-fd-complexes]. For every inclusion $E\subseteq L$, use the additive scalar-extension functor
$$
 T_{L/E}:D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)\longrightarrow D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(L),\qquad A\longmapsto A\otimes_E L
$$
of [def-weil-finite-dimensional-complex-scalar-extension]. This is induced by termwise exact tensor product on complexes, preserves quasi-isomorphisms and distinguished triangles, and has $H^i(T_{L/E}A)\cong H^i(A)\otimes_E L$. Use its shift comparison $\sigma_{L/E,A}:T_{L/E}(A[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(T_{L/E}A)[1]$. Write
$$
 c_{N/L/E}:T_{N/L}T_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{N/E},\qquad
 \iota_E:T_{E/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}
$$
for the tower and unit isomorphisms of [lem-weil-derived-field-scalar-extension-tower], restricted to these full subcategories. They obey the unit and four-field associativity equations and commute with the shift comparisons; the inclusions here and below allow equality of fields.

Define $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$ to be the following common-stage category. An object is a pair $(E,A)$ with $E\in\mathcal E_\ell$ and $A\in D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$. For $(E,A)$ and $(E',B)$ set
$$
 \operatorname{Hom}((E,A),(E',B))=
 \varinjlim_{L\in\mathcal E_\ell,\ L\supseteq E,E'}
 \operatorname{Hom}_{D(L)}(T_{L/E}A,T_{L/E'}B),
$$
the directed colimit of abelian groups [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]. The index is nonempty and directed: it contains $EE'$ and the compositum of any two of its fields. For $L\subseteq N$ the transition sends $u$ to
$$
 u_N=c_{N/L/E',B}\circ T_{N/L}(u)\circ c_{N/L/E,A}^{-1}.
$$
For $N=L$, the unit equation gives $c_{L/L/E,A}=\iota_{L,T_{L/E}A}$ and $c_{L/L/E',B}=\iota_{L,T_{L/E'}B}$. Thus $u_L=\iota_{L,T_{L/E'}B}\circ T_{L/L}(u)\circ\iota_{L,T_{L/E}A}^{-1}=u$ by naturality of $\iota_L$, as required for the identity transition of the directed system. A morphism is thus a class $[L,u]$, and $[L,u]=[L',v]$ means $u_N=v_N$ for some $N\supseteq L,L'$. Addition, negatives and zero are those of the displayed abelian-group colimit; explicitly $[L,u]+[L',v]=[N,u_N+v_N]$ at a common stage. The identity of $(E,A)$ is $[E,\operatorname{id}_{T_{E/E}A}]$. If $[L,u]:(E,A)\to(E',B)$ and $[L',v]:(E',B)\to(E'',C)$, define their composite to be $[N,v_N\circ u_N]$, for any $N\supseteq L,L'$. Coherence and naturality of $c$ give $(u_N)_P=u_P$ for $L\subseteq N\subseteq P$, and transition preserves sums, identities and composition. Consequently changing representatives or the common stage does not change these operations: transport all representatives to a common later stage and use these equations. The category identities, associativity and bilinearity then hold at that stage in $D(P)$. A zero object is $(\Ql,0)$. For two objects $(E,A)$ and $(E',B)$ choose $L\supseteq E,E'$ and take $(L,T_{L/E}A\oplus T_{L/E'}B)$ as a biproduct. Writing $S=T_{L/E}A\oplus T_{L/E'}B$ and $j_1,j_2,p_1,p_2$ for its biproduct maps in $D(L)$, the inclusions are represented at $L$ by $\iota_{L,S}^{-1}\circ j_1$ and $\iota_{L,S}^{-1}\circ j_2$, and the projections by $p_1\circ\iota_{L,S}$ and $p_2\circ\iota_{L,S}$. The biproduct equations hold at this stage and hence in the Hom colimits; thus the category is additive. The biproduct object lies in the required stage because its cohomology is the direct sum of the two bounded finite-dimensional cohomologies.

Define the shift on objects by $(E,A)[1]=(E,A[1])$, and on a morphism represented by $u$ over $L$ by
$$
 [L,u][1]=[L,\sigma_{L/E',B}^{-1}\circ u[1]\circ\sigma_{L/E,A}].
$$
The shift comparisons and their compatibility with $c$ make this independent of the representative. Its inverse is given by the same construction with $[-1]$. For each $L$, the stage functor $J_L:D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(L)\to D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$ sends $A$ to $(L,A)$ and $f$ to $[L,T_{L/L}(f)]$; the unit isomorphism $\iota_L$ supplies the identification with the usual stage inclusion. A triangle [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift] is distinguished precisely when it is isomorphic as a triangle to the image under $J_L$ of a distinguished triangle of $D(L)$ with all three vertices in $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(L)$, for some $L\in\mathcal E_\ell$; the last arrow uses the displayed shift identification $J_L(A[1])=J_L(A)[1]$.

This common-stage construction is the meaning of the blueprint notation $\operatorname{2-colim}_{E\in\mathcal E_\ell}D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$.

proof.text: Every object of PointFdQbar is its finite-field/object pair. Its original stage has exactly that object as image; the identity isomorphism proves EssSurjObj.

Apply [lem-weil-point-fd-morphism-descent] to the underlying realized morphism. Wrap the descended derived morphism in the finite-dimensional full subcategory. The definitions of the stage functor and of its tower comparison identify its image with the desired conjugation, proving HomSurj.

Prove faithfulness of actual derived scalar extension directly. Choose a K-linear functional p on L with p(1)=1 (Mathlib Module.Projective.exists_dual_eq_one). The map λ tensor m ↦ p(λ)m naturally retracts the extension/restriction adjunction unit. Apply these transformations termwise to complexes and descend along localization Q, using Localization.liftNatTrans, comp_liftNatTrans and liftNatTrans_id. They remain a natural retraction, so equality after extension and restriction implies equality by naturality and cancellation with the retraction. Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso identifies this functor with the composite of derived extension and restriction. Hence derived extension alone is faithful. In the finite-stage full subcategory equality is already detected at the original stage; apply its reflexive transition functor to equal maps to get HomInj. This proves all three fields of IsFilteredTwoColimit.

For shift stability use the homology shift-sequence isomorphism H^i(C[n]) ≅ H^(n+i)(C). Replace the original finite support s by the finite image of j ↦ j-n. If i is outside this image, n+i lies outside s, so H^i(C[n]) is zero by transport along that isomorphism. Finite dimension transfers along the same module isomorphism.
